runs.text: The Sudanese Arabs are the descendants of nomadic Bedouin who moved into the area from Saudi Arabia and inter-married with local African tribes. They are distinguished from other tribes in the area, in that their mother tongue is Sudanese Arabic, and they do not speak any tribal language. Some of them are still nomadic, and many of them live in rural areas, engaging in agriculture.

Sudan has been in a state of civil war since 2018. The two factions syphon off most of the aid money for themselves, often leaving the population without water or electricity. Due to the great instability, many people have been displaced both internally and externally. Outside of Sudan, the biggest population of Sudanese Arabs (4 million) is in Egypt.
Half of the population in Sudan is under 18, but a whole generation has received no or little schooling due to the political chaos.

Sudanese Arabs are Muslims, but witchcraft still plays a major role in their daily lives. Slowly, a few are coming to Christ through relationships and one-on-one discipleship. Sudan has many Christians, but the Church is cautious about reaching Muslims due to fear of government backlash. When Sudan split into north and south, 60% of Christian leaders moved to the South.
